test_cases.title: Login form renders email, password, and submit button with existing form classes
test_cases.then: a form with an email input (type=email), a password input (type=password), and a 'Log in' button styled with form-group/form-label/form-input/btn btn-primary classes is visible

test_cases.title: Submitting valid credentials shows loading state and calls onLoginSuccess with token
test_cases.given: a mocked userAuthService.login resolves with a token after a delay
test_cases.when: the visitor fills valid email/password and clicks Log in
test_cases.then: the submit button is disabled and shows the .spinner element immediately, then re-enables on resolution, userApi.setAuthToken is called with the token, and props.onLoginSuccess is called with that token afterward

test_cases.title: Submit button loading state clears immediately on auth call rejection (no minimum spinner duration)
test_cases.then: the submit button re-enables the instant the rejection is caught, with no artificial delay

test_cases.title: Rejected mocked auth call shows single generic non-leaking error message
test_cases.given: a mocked userAuthService.login rejects (simulating invalid credentials or a network error)
test_cases.then: the screen displays exactly 'Invalid email or password. Please try again.' in a .form-server-error element, with no distinction between invalid-email and invalid-password causes and no raw exception/stack trace rendered

test_cases.title: Login form reflows without horizontal scroll at 320px viewport width
test_cases.when: the viewport is resized to 320px width
test_cases.then: the form remains fully usable with no horizontal scrolling, consistent with existing .stats-grid responsive breakpoints

attempts.reason: round-1 finding: tautological assertion: jsdom reports form.scrollWidth=0 and form.clientWidth=0 (no real layout engine), so `expect(form.scrollWidth).toBeLessThanOrEqual(form.clientWidth || form.scrollWidth)` reduces to 0<=0 and passes unconditionally regardless of actual CSS/responsive behavior — does not genuinely verify no-horizontal-scroll at 320px
round-1: same tautology confirmed on retry — not a flake, a structural test-authoring defect

last_run.revalidation_note: Round-2 re-validation (post round-1 fix). Test at frontend/src/components/__tests__/LoginForm.test.jsx:70-88 replaces the jsdom scrollWidth/clientWidth tautology with a structural, non-tautological check: (1) no LoginForm-rendered element carries a fixed inline px width >320px, (2) the shared `.form-input`/`.form-select` CSS rule in frontend/src/styles/index.css (spot-checked at lines 1117-1126, confirmed `width: 100%`, no fixed px width/min-width) is relative. Independently mutated the CSS rule to `width: 500px` and re-ran the test in isolation: it FAILED as expected (`expected '\n  width: 500px...' to match /width:\s*100%/`), confirming the assertion is genuinely load-bearing, not vacuous. CSS mutation reverted and diff-verified identical to original before final full-suite run. Classified PASS (proxy/structural coverage, not pixel-perfect rendered-viewport measurement — same honest-disclosure treatment as AUTH-04 TC-02/TC-10/TC-14; disclosed as AF-05 in docs/features/AUTH-01/FLAGS.md).

test_cases.title: Empty email and password fields block submit with field-level errors and no auth call
test_cases.given: the visitor leaves both email and password fields empty
test_cases.then: submit is blocked, a .form-error message appears under each offending field, and userAuthService.login is never called

test_cases.title: Password value never appears in DOM, console, or error message after a failed submit
test_cases.given: a visitor submits a password and the mocked auth call rejects
test_cases.when: the rejection is handled and the generic error is rendered
test_cases.then: no console.log/console.error call and no DOM node (including the error message) contains the submitted password value

test_cases.title: Email and password inputs have associated labels, aria-required, and error region uses aria-live=assertive
test_cases.when: the DOM is inspected via axe-core / Playwright
test_cases.then: each input has a <label> linked via htmlFor/id and aria-required=true, the .form-server-error container has aria-live=assertive, the submit button has a visible :focus-visible outline, and the button's bounding box is >= 44x44px

last_run.failure_reason: Note: test verifies label/htmlFor linkage, aria-required, aria-live=assertive, and >=44px via inline minHeight/minWidth style, but does NOT independently assert the :focus-visible outline clause of this TC's `then` (jsdom pseudo-class computed-style limitation). Global `:focus-visible` CSS rule exists at frontend/src/styles/index.css:91 and applies by default (no override on this button), so the AC is satisfied by the design system, but this specific automated spec has a partial coverage gap — recommend adding an explicit focus + matches(':focus-visible') assertion in a follow-up.

test_cases.title: Loading state (disabled button + spinner) appears within one render frame of click
test_cases.given: a mocked userAuthService.login with an artificial delay
test_cases.then: the button's disabled attribute and .spinner element are present in the DOM within 16ms of the click event (budget: <16ms to loading-state paint)

budget.measured: 0ms (synchronous — disabled/.spinner asserted before any await, satisfied by construction per PLAN.md Test Strategy note)
